concepts.title: Tuple Aggregates: sum, min and max

questions.q: Evaluate tuple1.index(45) and tuple1.count(45) for the tuple (23, 1, 45, 67, 45, 9, 55, 45).. Use the method 'Tuple Aggregates: sum, min and max'. Work with: the fixed constants of the method. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of subtotal.

Find the total of all elements of the tuple (9, 8, 10, 12, 15).. Use the method 'Tuple Aggregates: sum, min and max'. Work with: the fixed constants of the method. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of subtotal.
Explain in your own words what 'Tuple Aggregates: sum, min and max' refers to.
questions.a: Built-in functions read a numeric tuple in one call: sum() totals its elements, min() returns the smallest and max() the largest, and sorted() hands back a brand-new sorted list without touching the tuple.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Tuple Aggregates: sum, min and max'.
questions.a: For the tuple (19, 12, 56, 18, 9, 87, 34) the three functions answer 235, 9 and 87.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Tuple Aggregates: sum, min and max', in plain ASCII form.
Using the method 'Swapping Numbers by Tuple Assignment', work with: first_value = 5000, second_value = 50000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of new_second.

Take the relation taught for 'Swapping Numbers by Tuple Assignment' and work with: first_value = 120000, second_value = 2500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of new_second.
Explain in your own words what 'Swapping Numbers by Tuple Assignment' refers to.
questions.a: Tuple assignment places a tuple of variables on the left of = and values on the right, so two numbers swap without a temporary variable; the counts on both sides must match or a ValueError about unpacking appears.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Swapping Numbers by Tuple Assignment'.
questions.a: The right side is fully evaluated before any assignment, which is why no value is lost during the swap.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Swapping Numbers by Tuple Assignment', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Circle Area and Circumference Returned as a Tuple

questions.q: Using the method 'Circle Area and Circumference Returned as a Tuple', work with: radius = 400. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of circumference.
Take the relation taught for 'Circle Area and Circumference Returned as a Tuple' and work with: radius = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of circumference.
Explain in your own words what 'Circle Area and Circumference Returned as a Tuple' refers to.
questions.a: The function circle(r) computes both the area (3.14 times radius squared) and the circumference (2 times 3.14 times radius), then returns them together as a two-element tuple that the caller unpacks in one statement.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Circle Area and Circumference Returned as a Tuple'.
questions.a: Returning (area, circumference) lets one function deliver two results without global variables.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Circle Area and Circumference Returned as a Tuple', in plain ASCII form.
Using the method 'Aggregating Dictionary Values', work with: the fixed constants of the method. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of average.
Take the relation taught for 'Aggregating Dictionary Values' and work with: the fixed constants of the method. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of average.
Explain in your own words what 'Aggregating Dictionary Values' refers to.
questions.a: A dictionary maps unique keys to values, and the methods values() and items() expose the stored data; the marks of a class dictionary can be totalled and averaged by reading the value of every key.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Aggregating Dictionary Values'.
questions.a: Keys act as the index, so dict3['Ram'] always yields 89 no matter where the item sits.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Aggregating Dictionary Values', in plain ASCII form.
Using the method 'Character Frequency Dictionary', work with: total_letters = 120, distinct_letters = 7. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of extra_copies.
Take the relation taught for 'Character Frequency Dictionary' and work with: total_letters = 20, distinct_letters = 7. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of extra_copies.
Explain in your own words what 'Character Frequency Dictionary' refers to.
questions.a: Traversing a string with a dictionary counter tallies each character: the first sighting stores 1 under that key and every later sighting increments it, so the dictionary maps each character to how many times it occurs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Character Frequency Dictionary'.
questions.a: For 'HelloWorld' the counter shows l at 3 and o at 2, and every other letter exactly once.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Character Frequency Dictionary', in plain ASCII form.
Using the method 'Single-Element Tuple Comma Rule', work with: comma = 25, marks = 8, the = 60, tuple = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of tuple5.
Take the relation taught for 'Single-Element Tuple Comma Rule' and work with: comma = 24, marks = 30, the = 100, tuple = 6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of tuple5.
Explain in your own words what 'Single-Element Tuple Comma Rule' refers to.
questions.a: A tuple holding exactly one element still needs a trailing comma: (20) is merely the integer 20 in brackets, while (20,) is a tuple; even without parentheses, comma-separated values such as 1, 2, 3 form a tuple.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Single-Element Tuple Comma Rule'.
questions.a: The comma, not the parenthesis, is what makes a tuple.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Single-Element Tuple Comma Rule', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Immutable Tuple with a Mutable List Inside

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Immutable Tuple with a Mutable List Inside' refers to.
questions.a: Assigning to a tuple position raises TypeError because a tuple is immutable, yet a list stored inside the tuple remains editable through two indices, so tuple2[3][1] = 10 succeeds while tuple2[3] = something does not.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Immutable Tuple with a Mutable List Inside'.
questions.a: Immutability freezes the references a tuple holds, not the contents those references point to.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Immutable Tuple with a Mutable List Inside', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Dictionary Methods: get, update, del and clear

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Dictionary Methods: get, update, del and clear' refers to.
questions.a: The get() method fetches a value or falls back to None for a missing key, update() merges another dictionary's pairs in, del removes one key's item or the whole dictionary, and clear() empties every pair while keeping the name alive.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Dictionary Methods: get, update, del and clear'.
questions.a: After del dict1 the name itself is gone and reuse raises NameError, but after clear() the empty dictionary remains.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Dictionary Methods: get, update, del and clear', in plain ASCII form.
